categories.main_business_segments: Zscaler operates as a single reportable segment focused on providing cloud-based security solutions. Its core business is the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform, which delivers integrated security services for users, workloads, and devices across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments. The company’s offerings are organized around four solution pillars: Zero Trust Everywhere, Data Security Everywhere, Security for AI, and Agentic Operations.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Zscaler’s platform is built on a cloud-native, multi-tenant architecture distributed across more than 160 public exchanges and thousands of private edge exchanges globally. The platform leverages advanced AI and machine learning for threat detection, inline inspection, and policy enforcement, and is protected by over 725 issued and pending patents. Key technologies include proxy-based security, TLS/SSL inspection, cloud sandboxing, browser isolation, microsegmentation, and AI-powered data classification.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Zscaler serves over 9,400 customers, with a focus on large enterprises and government agencies, including approximately 40% of the Forbes Global 2000 and over 45% of Fortune 500 companies. Its customer base spans industries such as financial services, healthcare, insurance, manufacturing, automotive, transportation, retail, media, public sector, education, energy, technology, and telecommunications. The company primarily targets organizations undergoing digital transformation and cloud adoption.
categories.geographic_coverage: Zscaler operates in over 185 countries, with approximately 49% of revenue generated outside the United States. Key regions include North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia Pacific, with ongoing expansion into Latin America and the Middle East. The company maintains a global presence with offices and data centers across these regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: Zscaler operates downstream in the cybersecurity supply chain, delivering cloud-based security services directly to end customers and through channel partners. It acts as a service provider, integrating with upstream technology vendors and infrastructure providers, and is positioned at the point of user, device, and application access to networks and cloud resources.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Zscaler’s strategic priorities center on expanding its Zero Trust platform, integrating advanced AI and machine learning, and addressing emerging security challenges related to cloud, mobility, and AI adoption. The company invests heavily in R&D (over $672 million in FY25) to enhance platform functionality, scalability, and reliability, and to develop new solutions for AI security, data protection, and agentic operations. Growth strategies include winning new customers, expanding within existing accounts, leveraging channel partnerships, and entering new geographic and vertical markets.
categories.revenue_model: Zscaler generates revenue primarily through subscription-based sales of its cloud security platform and related support services, with contracts typically ranging from one to three years. Subscription pricing is primarily calculated on a per-user basis, and revenue is recognized ratably over the contract term. A small portion of revenue comes from professional services such as implementation and training.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Zscaler competes with legacy on-premises security vendors, large networking companies, and point-solution providers in areas such as firewalls, VPNs, CASB, sandboxing, and DLP. Key competitors include Palo Alto Networks, Cisco, Fortinet, Symantec (Broadcom), and emerging cloud security vendors. Zscaler differentiates itself as a pioneer in cloud-native, integrated Zero Trust security, but faces competition from larger firms with broader portfolios and greater resources.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended July 31, 2025, Zscaler reported revenue of $2.67 billion, up 23% from $2.17 billion in 2024 and $1.62 billion in 2023, reflecting strong double-digit growth. The company had a net loss of $41.5 million in 2025, continuing a trend of annual net losses as it invests for growth. Zscaler’s market capitalization was approximately $17.9 billion as of January 2025, and it maintains a robust cash position with $3.57 billion in cash and investments.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Zscaler’s value proposition centers on enabling secure digital transformation through a cloud-native, scalable, and integrated Zero Trust platform. The company emphasizes rapid threat detection and response, AI-driven security, seamless user experience, and reduced complexity and cost compared to legacy appliance-based solutions. Its ability to deliver security at scale, with continuous updates and global reach, is a key differentiator, as is its focus on securing AI applications and agentic operations.
